keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 199-206: the End of the Han page: Sun Ce 'conquered several territories in Jiangdong between 194 and 199'; the Sun Ce page has him appointing relatives and a trusted subject 'to govern Danyang and Yuzhang', Luling divided from them, and Wan County captured after Yuan Shu's death in 199. The Eastern Wu page gives no territory for 200-209. Cliopatria's Eastern Wu shape for 207 (609,286 km2) is the matching state; the real state is continuous with Sun Quan's Wu (the Eastern Wu page: Sun Quan 'King of Wu' to 229). Repair pass: Wu Commandery is in this shape too. The Sun Quan page dates Yuzhang to 199 ('In 199, Sun Quan followed his brother to conquer Lujiang and Yuzhang'); the Hua Xin page (Administrator of Yuzhang 192-199 in its infobox) says only that he 'joined the forces of Sun Ce'; Luling is undated on all pages.

ledger.note: 195: Sun Ce holds Niuzhu and Danyang under Yuan Shu. 'In 194 Sun Ce went to Yuan Shu' (infobox allegiance: Yuan Shu's forces); the offensive across the Yangtze that took Niuzhu is 195, so the tie is entered with the foothold. The yuan-shu dossier dates the same tie to 195.

region.text: Kuaiji, Sun Ce's base city, whose governor Wang Lang surrendered

ledger.note: 196: Kuaiji. Sun Ce 'pushed into Yang Province and conquered Kuaiji, whose governor Wang Lang surrendered' and 'made Kuaiji his base city'; the page dates no surrender. The conquest of 'the entire region southeast of the Long River' took 'less than a year' from Niuzhu (195), so 196 is the ceiling; the infobox gives him as Administrator of Kuaiji 197-198 (an office date, which was why this event stood at 197 before the repair pass).

region.text: Wu Commandery (Suzhou-Wuxi, southern Jiangsu), whose former administrator Xu Gong 'had long opposed Sun Ce'; part of 'the entire region southeast of the Long River' conquered 'in less than a year' from Niuzhu

ledger.note: 196: Wu Commandery (Suzhou-Wuxi). The page does not name the conquest of Wu in a dated sentence; it says the conquest of 'the entire region southeast of the Long River' took 'less than a year' from Niuzhu (195) and that Xu Gong, 'the former administrator of Wu Commandery', 'had long opposed Sun Ce'. The year is the page's ceiling (196) and the region is the page's wording read as the three commanderies, hence confidence 2.

After Yuan Shu's death in 199 Sun Ce 'captured the poorly-defended Wan County' (Lujiang), and Danyang, Yuzhang and the new Luling commandery were governed by his relatives and a trusted subject; the page gives no year for Yuzhang and Luling, so the whole of Jiangxi is entered at 199 by the End of the Han page's 'between 194 and 199'. ledger.note: 206: the Jiangdong of Sun Ce and Sun Quan passes into Cliopatria's Eastern Wu row, which starts in 207. Sun Ce was assassinated on 5 May 200 and 'succeeded by his younger brother, Sun Quan'; the opened pages date no event in 201-206, so the end year is a bridging choice (confidence 1) for the join with Eastern Wu. Sun Quan page (opened in the repair pass): in 200 he 'inherited the lands southeast of the Yangtze River from his brother' (no commandery list); 'In 206, he conquered the fortress of Shanyue in Matun and Baodun'; 'In 208 ... he obtained most of the territory of Jiangxia' (after Huang Zu's death), which is Eastern Wu's, not this dossier's. The page names no 201-206 border change, so 206 stays a bridge.

notes:
Sun Ce, Jiangdong 195-206. 3 pages opened (Sun Ce, Eastern Wu, End of the Han dynasty); no Cliopatria row. The state is the early Wu of Sun Ce and Sun Quan: ea-03 should decide whether to extend eastern-wu back to 195; if so this dossier is dropped and its events moved.
Unsettled: (1) the Sun Ce page dates only the crossing (195), the Kuaiji office in the infobox (197-198) and the death (5 May 200); Yuzhang, Luling, Lujiang and Wan County (199) are not dated beyond 'between 194 and 199'; (2) Wang Lang, Liu Yao, Yan Baihu and Xu Gong were Han officials or bandit leaders, not states; (3) 206 as end is a bridge to the Cliopatria row at 207: no page dates anything 201-206; (4) the Eastern Wu page gives no 200-209 territory or the Huang Zu fight over Jiangxia; (5) Wuhu, Nanjing, Anqing circles and the two modern provinces stand for the commanderies.
Counterparts: han-dynasty and eastern-wu exist; Yuan Shu (Sun Ce's former master, south of the Huai) has no dossier.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): 5 pages now (Sun Ce, End of the Han dynasty, Eastern Wu, Hua Xin, Sun Quan), the budget for a state without a Cliopatria row. (1) Wu Commandery (Suzhou, Jiangsu 100 km) added from 196 and Kuaiji moved from 197 to 196 on the Sun Ce page's 'less than a year' from Niuzhu (195); both confidence 2 (no dated sentence). (2) vassal_start 195 and vassal_end 197 with yuan-shu added (the Sun Ce page: Yuan Shu in 194, break in 197); yuan-shu mirrors them. (3) Yuzhang is dated 199 by the Sun Quan page; Luling and the rest of Jiangxi remain a reading. (4) The 206 end stays a bridge: the Sun Quan page names the Shanyue fortress in 206 and Huang Zu's death in 208 (Jiangxia) but no commandery change for 201-206. Place name: 'Suzhou, Jiangsu' (the gazetteer's alias for the Jiangsu Suzhou; plain 'Suzhou' resolves to Suzhou in Anhui).
